title: Summer Games II
build: US Gold's two-disk PAL release, as two G64 images: a BASIC boot file, a fast loader that stays at $0800-$0FFF, and fourteen packed modules read by one-letter names: the menu, the title, two ceremonies, eight events, and the first Summer Games' swimming events on side 2. Each part has its own listing

Entry: maps in the RAM under BASIC, sets the raster interrupt and the stadium, silences the SID, starts the tune, then waits for the tune to end or for a joystick to be let go and pressed again, and returns to the loader.
The wait: a press counts only after one release, so a button still held from the menu does not skip the ceremony.
The interrupt at line $FB: plays the tune, sets the eight sprites for the upper screen from the doves' table, then runs the step of the ceremony: the bearer running, the lighting, or the doves.
To the lighting.

On the steps, between x $58 and $E4, lifts the bearer a pixel on the frames of the stride that push up.
Places the bearer's sprites and the torch with him.
Makes the flame flicker by writing random bytes into its sprite, and picks the flame's frame every eight frames.
Each of the eight doves: climbs a line on its own delay, drifts right at its own speed, flaps through its wingbeat, and is turned off once above line $5C.
Restores the registers and returns from the interrupt.
